propositions: A rejected auto-push succeeds locally and reports success to the caller while the remote rejects the branch, leaving the write appearing shared when it is actually diverged.

Git stderr containing policy-decline markers (hook declined, push declined, protected branch, rate limit, internal server error) is misclassified by _NON_FF regex as a retriable non-fast-forward, causing three futile retries and discarding the rejection reason.

The PUSH_PENDING divergence signal is computed only by fsck (a pull operation) and never re-announced by write commands, so a rejection persists silently across the command invocations that follow it.
Ticket event payloads (comments containing environment output or credentials) are not scanned for secrets on write, unlike code which is scanned by gitleaks in the review gate.
The unpushed-commit backlog count is not included in push-failure warnings, so identical one-line messages give no indication of an escalating divergence even if the failure is eventually seen.

On sync.push=async or in library/MCP contexts the push warning is routed to /dev/null or the server's stderr rather than the writing agent's stderr, making the failure completely invisible to the caller.
